title: Cover and Cipher Anew
premise: Rosalind Thackeray, a whistle-blower who has survived four identities and one burned network, receives a calendar invite from his dead handler, Mara Voss, scheduling a meeting twenty-four hours out. Following the thread, he uncovers a plot to destroy a ferry terminal with a rigged gas leak—an 'accident' designed to bury evidence of the program he once exposed, along with him. To stop it, he must reunite the scattered remnants of his old team, people who have every reason to hate him, and accept that the found family he abandoned is the only inheritance worth claiming. The attack is averted at cost: Rosalind surrenders his anonymity, testifies under his real name, and finally stops running.
about_author: Orsen Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who spent a decade writing safety reports no one read before turning to fiction. He lives in a coastal town he refuses to name, and writes about people who can't go home again.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, living quietly as 'Daniel Reeve' in a rain-soaked port town. His carefully maintained routine shatters when an email arrives from Mara Voss—dead eleven months—inviting him to meet tomorrow at 9 p.m. He verifies it's not phishing, then finds her old dead-drop signal freshly chalked. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant hope that she might be alive.

chapters.title: Four Names Deep
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, flashback-woven. He audits his own tradecraft while deciding whether to go: four names, four cities, one packed go-bag by the door for six years. He digs up Mara's last case file and finds a ferry terminal flagged for 'infrastructure review.' Emotional beat: the loneliness of witness protection of one's own making.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind at the meeting site. No Mara—instead a burner phone with a voice message she recorded before dying, warning of an operation called LOW TIDE and naming the terminal. He's spotted by a watcher and barely escapes. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; Mara reached beyond the grave because she trusted only him.

chapters.title: The People He Burned
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind and Priya Nair, his former analyst now running a dive bar and hating him for vanishing. Rosalind asks for help; she throws him out—but pockets the terminal schematic he leaves behind. Emotional beat: guilt meeting resentment; belonging offered and refused.

chapters.title: LOW TIDE
chapters.summary: POV Priya. She decrypts the schematic and realizes the 'gas leak' scenario maps perfectly onto the ferry terminal's maintenance schedule—three days out. She contacts Rosalind on her terms. Meanwhile a second team member, ex-security chief Tomas Reyes, is already asking questions in town. Emotional beat: anger transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Reunion of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The old cell reconvenes in Priya's back room: Priya, Reyes, and hacker Jules Okonkwo, who was imprisoned because of Rosalind's escape plan. Old wounds are aired over maps and timers. They discover the 'accident' would also destroy archived records proving who ordered the original cover-up. Emotional beat: fractured family choosing to try again.

chapters.title: What Inheritance Buys
chapters.summary: POV Jules. Digging into LOW TIDE's funding, Jules traces it to Halcyon Maritime—the company Rosalind exposed—and its still-protected director, Edmund Voss, Mara's brother. The attack isn't revenge; it's estate management, erasing liability. A tail nearly catches Jules. Emotional beat: the horror of inheritance as erasure, and personal stakes sharpening.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. Recon confirms the device is planted in the pump house; disarm codes require access only Voss's people hold. The team splits: Priya and Jules on the records vault, Rosalind and Reyes on the pump house. A betrayal hint surfaces—someone leaked their timeline. Emotional beat: trust tested at the worst possible hour.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, climax. Inside the pump house he confronts the saboteur—Mara's old protégé, coerced by Voss—and talks him down while Reyes races the failsafe timer. The bomb is neutralized with ninety seconds left; the vault team secures copies of the records. Voss is arrested at the dock trying to flee. Emotional beat: terror, sacrifice, and the choice to be seen.

chapters.title: Rosalind Thackeray
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, resolution. He gives his real name to investigators and the press, ending four names' worth of hiding. The team gathers at Priya's bar—not a unit anymore, but something better: a family that chose itself twice. He unpacks the go-bag at last. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging; inheritance reclaimed as memory instead of fear.
